ContentSkeletonElement.description: A node of the skeleton format's element tree: structure only, with every property value stripped. The skeleton is a function of structure alone, so the same layout and request produce the same skeleton whatever data resolution found. This is the skeleton format's node and only that — the decomposed format serves its own node shape (`ContentDecomposedElement`) with a different grammar for `apiAlias`.

id.description: Element identifier, carried through from the stored element. Unique across every root of the page.

component.description: Element component type (e.g. Sw:Grid:Container, Sw:Content:Text, Sw:Media:Image).

slots.description: Child element subtrees keyed by slot name, each slot holding an ordered list of child skeleton nodes. Always present on every node at every depth, and a node with no slots carries it as an empty JSON array `[]` rather than an empty object. `ContentDecomposedElement` states the same grammar; the two node types differ on `apiAlias` placement, not on this key.

oneOf.description: The empty slot map, serialized as `[]`.

style.description: Universal presentation options keyed by option wire name, carried through from the stored element. Each value is either a single scalar (a flat option) or an object keyed by breakpoint (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl) for a breakpoint-aware option, per the option's breakpointAware flag in the style-option introspection schema. Omitted when the element has no style.

apiAlias.description: Present on ROOT elements only. The alias is appended by the framework struct encoder, which runs at the response root, so nested nodes inside `slots` do not carry it. A recursive schema cannot express a root-only member structurally, so it is declared optional here; the contract is that it appears on the elements of the page's `elements` array and on no node below them.
